title: The xFPL codebase, as the CTO knows it
body:
Snapshot taken 3 September 2026 from the repository. Refreshed when a session regenerates it - it is the shape of the code, not today's exact contents of a given function.

SHAPE: a monorepo. backend/ is FastAPI + Python 3.12 (69 modules, 9,692 lines in the app package; ~13,400 with tools and tests). frontend/ is Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript / Tailwind v4 (~18,800 lines). data/ holds committed FPL snapshots, the frozen projections and the published accuracy record (~12 MB).

LAYERING, strictly one-directional: api/routers -> services -> domain | model | optimize -> data.

THE LARGEST MODULES, with lines:
  model/predict.py 634 - per-fixture points decomposition, the cached prediction context, single and multi-gameweek entry points
  services/players.py 614 - player list, detail, trajectory, alternatives, comparison
  domain/scoring.py 477 - recommendation_score, the hand-weighted heuristic (NEVER BACKTESTED)
  optimize/squad.py 374 - the ILP squad and transfer optimiser, PuLP/CBC
  data/ingest/pipeline.py 350 - hourly ingest and snapshot pruning
  model/distribution.py 332 - the outcome distribution behind a projection; haul probability and ceiling, enumerated analytically not simulated
  services/season_run.py 326 - the model playing its own season
  domain/accuracy.py 319 - grading a finished gameweek against what happened
  optimize/horizon.py 276 - transfers planned across a window, not one week at a time
  model/strengths.py 265 - Dixon-Coles team strengths, cross-season blending, the team-id remap
  model/involvement.py 260 - player share of team output, appearance probabilities, personal rates
  model/rules.py 207 - FPL scoring constants and every calibration parameter, each with the evidence that chose it

THE API: 33 routes across 7 routers (health, players, teams, fixtures, optimizer, squad, leagues). Route-keyed Cache-Control policy table defaulting to no-store.

THE DATABASE: PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic. Three tables - raw_snapshots (JSONB), player_gw_stats, ingest_runs. DB-first with an on-disk file fallback, which is why losing the free Postgres never took the site down.

TESTING: 178 backend tests, CI green on main. Golden response snapshots pin API responses byte-for-byte AND generate the frontend's TypeScript types, so the two cannot drift. Gates: pytest in backend/; npm run gen:api, npx tsc --noEmit, npx eslint src --max-warnings 0, npm run build in frontend/.

SCHEDULING, all on GitHub Actions, all free: hourly ingest; projection freeze 4x/day; freshness check every 6h; keep-alive every 10 min; weekly fallback-snapshot PR.

THE DANGEROUS AREAS:
1. Season transitions. FPL reassigns team and element IDs alphabetically each season. Mixing an archived file with a live one silently attaches the wrong team's fixtures to a player. Guarded by explicit name/code remaps and paired bootstrap_file/fixtures_file parameters. Treat any change near these as high-risk.
2. Determinism. Golden tests pin exact bytes; a randomised request path breaks CI on a different CPU. This is why the distribution is enumerated rather than simulated.
3. alembic/env.py sets target_metadata to xFPL's models alone - a second application sharing that database would have the next autogenerate propose dropping its tables.

KNOWN DEBT: the README (776 lines) describes analysis.py, team_model.py, my_squad.py and chip_strategy.py - none exist - and states "No dark mode" for an app that is dark by default. docs/FRONTEND_REFACTOR_PLAN.md says "nothing here is executed yet" and is fully executed. anthropic==0.118.0 is pinned in requirements.txt and never imported. API_FOOTBALL_KEY is plumbed through render.yaml and .env.example and never read. BuildSquadPanel is 826 lines, LoadTeamPanel 655, OptimizePanel 496.

NO observability: no error tracking on either tier, no uptime alerting beyond the 6-hourly data-freshness workflow.
